name: Ionizing threshold wavelength
meaning: A photon must have at least about 10 eV (wavelength about 124 nm or shorter) to ionize; λ in nm, E in eV.

name: Equivalent dose
meaning: Biologically weighted dose H (Sv) equals the radiation weighting factor w_R (dimensionless) times the absorbed dose D (Gy = J/kg).

name: Inverse-square law
meaning: Intensity (W/m² or dose rate) from a point source falls as 1/distance²; P is source power (W), r distance (m).

name: Exponential attenuation
meaning: Photon intensity after thickness x (cm) of shield; μ is the linear attenuation coefficient (cm⁻¹), μ/ρ the mass attenuation coefficient (cm²/g), ρ the density (g/cm³).

name: Half-value layer
meaning: Thickness (cm) that halves a photon beam; n half-value layers transmit (1/2)^n.

name: Lorentz (magnetic) force
meaning: Force (N) on charge q (C) moving with velocity v (m/s) in magnetic field B (T). It is perpendicular to v, so it changes direction but not speed; zero for uncharged photons and neutrons.

name: Gyroradius
meaning: Radius (m) of a charged particle's circular or helical path; m mass (kg), v speed perpendicular to B (m/s). Near light speed, replace mv with the relativistic momentum p.
